critical_code_review_comments: webhooks_payment._extract_external_event_id: the Razorpay branch composes 'rzp:{event}:{payment_id}:{created_at}' only if ALL THREE components are present — otherwise falls back to body-hash. This is the right conservative choice; a partial composite (e.g., rzp:payment.captured:pay_XYZ without created_at) would still silently collide across events. Consider adding a debug log line when the Razorpay fallback fires so operators can see when created_at is unexpectedly absent from vendor payloads.

webhooks_email._SERVER_MISCONFIG_PREFIX now includes 'cryptography_missing' and 'bad_key_or_signature'. The naming is slightly overloaded — 'bad_key_or_signature' is a compound reason that covers BOTH an operator-pasted-bad-PEM case (503) AND a genuinely malformed signature (arguably 400). The verifier currently emits this as a single code; if you later split the SendGrid ECDSA verifier into 'operator_bad_pem' vs 'signature_mismatch' you'll get a cleaner 503/400 split. Non-blocking.

webhooks_payment._SERVER_MISCONFIG_PREFIX includes 'verify_failed' — this collapses TWO distinct upstream conditions into 503: (a) PayPal verify endpoint returned HTTP 5xx (transient upstream) and (b) verify endpoint returned HTTP 2xx with body {verification_status:FAILURE} (semantic fail). Case (b) is technically a signature mismatch that COULD indicate a client replay attack, but distinguishing them requires the verifier to emit 'verify_failed:FAILURE' vs 'verify_failed:HTTP N'. Current mapping treats all as 503 which is safe (never 500) but slightly muddles the operator health signal. Consider a follow-up refinement.

Race-guard pattern (try insert_one / except DuplicateKeyError / re-read row) is now duplicated verbatim across webhooks_email.py and webhooks_payment.py. When a third webhook category lands (e.g., SMS/WhatsApp inbound), extract to a shared helper in core/webhook_dedup.py to avoid drift.
